Summary:  
The paper introduces an offline imitation-learning (IL) algorithm that learns an expert-level policy from datasets largely composed of sub-optimal demonstrations. The core contribution is a cooperative training framework in which a discriminator distinguishes expert from non-expert data and its confidence scores weight the behavioural-cloning (BC) loss, eliminating the need for an explicit reward model or offline RL fine-tuning.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]

Inference-strategy justification:  
All nodes are grounded in explicit statements (motivation, method, results). Moderate inference (confidence = 2) was only used to articulate AI-safety-relevant risks (deployment of sub-optimal policies) and to map the algorithm to an actionable intervention node.

Extraction completeness explanation:  
The fabric contains the full causal chain from the identified risk through two problem analyses, two theoretical insights, a design rationale, an implementation mechanism, validation evidence and a concrete intervention. All nodes are interconnected; no isolated nodes remain.

Key limitations:  
1. The paper focuses on performance, not explicit safety metrics; risk framing therefore required moderate inference.  
2. Experimental evidence is limited to standard benchmarks; generalisability to real-world safety-critical domains is uncertain.  
3. Section titles in the short abstract were inferred (“Introduction”, “Method”, “Experiments”); future access to the full text would improve citation accuracy.
